command_template: python3 tools/debian_native_container_probe.py CLIENT VERIFIED_DEB DEB_SHA256 VERIFIED_SKILL_ZIP SKILL_SHA256 --fixture-mode client-control-cancellation --container-memory-mib 128 --sample-server-resources
fixture: Route-free DNS and HTTP. Native client begins GET /cancel-drip; control API interruption is issued after fixture starts; approved /plain recovery, loopback denial and approved HEAD follow.
limitations: Claude Code emitted one matching MCP cancellation notification and the server closed the socket promptly; Codex app-server turn/interrupt acknowledged the interruption but emitted no MCP cancellation notification in this run. Its pending fetch returned EGRESS_RESPONSE_TOO_SLOW, then the socket closed after about three seconds. This is a client control-path gap, not a successful wire cancellation.
The skill ZIP checksum was verified but this control-path mode did not load or invoke the skill. The clients ran on Ubuntu while the server ran in Debian 12 amd64.

Server /proc RSS and FD readings are finite 50 ms samples and can miss transient peaks. Container cgroup peaks include setup/helpers. No saturated queue, repeated cancellation, aggregate resource bound, Cursor, terminal/desktop UI cancellation, or traffic sent via other tools was tested.
Package is experimental and unsigned, not an approved official candidate; owner review and residual-risk acceptance remain open.
